facts.label: Leverage and coverage
facts.text: Leverage on carrying-value debt fell from 8.89x at the end of 2024 to 5.77x at the end of 2025 and 5.00x at 30 September 2026. The 2024 ratio is not like-for-like: that debt also funded the Alkali business, sold in February 2025 and shown as discontinued, while the EBITDA covers continuing operations only. Gross debt rose in 2026, so the fall to the latest ratio rests on higher earnings over the last twelve months, which creditors need to see sustained, rather than on repayment. Cash interest cover rose from 1.43x in FY2024 to 1.87x in FY2025 and 2.41x on the last twelve months, against a minimum covenant of 2.00x that is measured on the credit agreement's own definitions and therefore cannot be tested from these figures. Action: obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release. - High: no 2026 document states compliance with the issuer's financial covenants or reports the interest coverage and senior secured leverage ratios, and the executed credit agreement is not supplied, so covenant headroom is not calculable. Action: obtain the credit agreement and a compliance certificate. - Medium: the revolver's collateral and its rank against the senior unsecured notes are not stated in any supplied document, so the revolver is left out of the debt stack; it is undrawn at 2026-09-30. Action: obtain the credit agreement. - Medium: availability under the revolver at 2024-12-31 is not stated, so the 2024 liquidity row has cash only; no balance sheet at 2023-12-31 or 2025-09-30 is supplied, so those columns are not supplied. Action: obtain the 2024 annual report and the third-quarter 2025 quarterly report. - Medium: where a source prints a dash, the table shows not supplied rather than zero; this affects impairment expense, the gain on sale of assets, discontinued-operations lines, the equity investee investments in 2025, the receivables facility and restricted cash before 2026, and several cash flow lines in periods where they are not printed. Action: none needed unless a nil amount is confirmed. - Medium: cash interest paid is printed in millions to one decimal, so the thousands digits in the cash flow table are zero by rounding, and the FY2025 and nine-month 2025 amounts include the discontinued Alkali business to 2025-02-28. Action: obtain the interest paid detail if exact amounts are needed. - Medium: the Adjusted EBITDA for the nine months of 2025 includes the discontinued Alkali business and the nine months of 2026 keeps a gain of USD 17,436 thousand, so neither is comparable with continuing-operations EBITDA. Action: treat them as issuer-reported only. - Low: scheduled amortisation of the notes, the interest rate floors on the revolver and receivables facility, and the Genesis Energy Finance Corporation statements are not stated. Action: obtain the indentures and the credit agreement. - Low: the guidance range for 2026 Adjusted EBITDA in dollars and the year-end call are not supplied, and no amount is stated for the early-October hurricane disruption. Action: obtain the year-end call text and the October event disclosure. - Low: Q4 2025 is not stated on its own and the fourth-quarter 2025 earnings release is not supplied; a fourth quarter can only be derived as the full year less nine months. Action: obtain the release.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: - Cash conversion has improved because growth spending ended, but working capital flatters the latest year. facts.label: Company description and credit linkage
facts.text: Genesis Energy is a Houston-based midstream partnership that earns fees in three businesses: offshore crude oil and natural gas pipelines in the Gulf of America, a U.S.-flag Jones Act marine fleet, and onshore crude pipelines with sulfur services on the Gulf Coast. Offshore fees are charged per barrel or under capacity arrangements that limit direct exposure to commodity prices, most production handled is under life-of-lease commitments, and 77% of marine revenue was on term contracts in FY2025. That gives the group visible cash flow while producers keep producing, but only about 27.51% of last-twelve-months offshore revenue is fixed or minimum-based for 2027, so visibility fades after 2028. Onshore revenue is largely crude marketing sales that carry thin margins. Debt service capacity is therefore supported by the offshore fee stream, liquidity is preserved by the end of growth spending, and refinancing confidence depends on offshore volumes holding while leverage is above 5x. facts.label: Ownership and group structure
facts.text: Genesis Energy, L.P. is a listed partnership whose general partner it owns outright. Class B units elect the whole board, one family holds 76.9% of them and can appoint up to three directors, and holders of the preferred units keep a board observer right while they hold enough of the class. The partnership has chosen not to follow listing rules on independent nominating and compensation committees. The notes are guaranteed by the domestic guarantor subsidiaries, while the receivables facility sits in a bankruptcy-remote vehicle outside the guarantor group and its receivables are not available to other creditors. A financial party owns the remaining 36% of CHOPS and the consolidated Independence Hub also carries a noncontrolling interest, so part of consolidated EBITDA leaves the group as distributions to those holders. The credit implication is that control is concentrated, creditors have no governance voice, the 2026 pattern favours equity returns, and the structurally senior claims are the USD 99.5 million receivables facility and minority distributions equal to 11.32% of EBITDA. The notes are guaranteed by the domestic guarantor subsidiaries, while the receivables facility sits in a bankruptcy-remote vehicle outside the guarantor group and its receivables are not available to other creditors. A financial party owns the remaining 36% of CHOPS and the consolidated Independence Hub also carries a noncontrolling interest, so part of consolidated EBITDA leaves the group as distributions to those holders. The credit implication is that control is concentrated, creditors have no governance voice, the 2026 pattern favours equity returns, and the structurally senior claims are the USD 99.5 million receivables facility and minority distributions equal to 11.32% of EBITDA.

facts.label: Revenue drivers and pricing power
facts.text: Offshore revenue is volume-driven: fees are fixed per unit of volume under contracts or regulated tariffs, some contracts add capacity-reservation fees, and tiered fees step with cumulative throughput, so earnings follow producers' well performance and the number of rigs that can drill. The mechanism showed in the third quarter, when oil volumes were 0.99% lower and gas volumes 31.98% lower than a year earlier, Shenandoah fell below its minimum commitment and offshore Segment Margin fell 3.50%, although nine-month oil volumes were still 13.26% higher. For credit, offshore revenue is partly predictable through 2028, cyclical with drilling activity, concentrated by field, and exposed to hurricanes; pricing is set by contract and tariff, so growth comes from volume rather than price. Marine revenue is 77% term and 23% spot, utilization is near full and management reports robust spot rates, which supports renewals. Onshore pipeline volumes rose 35.49% in the third quarter, and the sulfur business holds 11 contracts with about two years remaining on average, so onshore is recurring in part but its upside is tied to dislocations. No single customer exceeded 10% of revenue in 2025, although Shell reached 11% in 2024, so customer concentration is moderate and the larger concentration is in producers behind a few fields. facts.label: Cost structure and margin resilience
facts.text: The offshore cost base is small relative to revenue and, on the evidence of a steady margin, largely fixed, so revenue less operating costs held between 71.05% and 74.87% of revenue from FY2023 to the last twelve months; that margin can be defended under volume pressure only until volumes fall below minimum commitments, after which each lost barrel falls almost entirely to EBITDA. Marine margin after operating costs slipped from 38.87% in FY2024 to 33.52% over the last twelve months; nine-month Segment Margin fell 3.70% on planned dry-docking days, although the third quarter rose 12.16%, and rebilled fuel and other costs that pass through enlarge revenue and costs together, so the percentage understates cash margin. The 23% spot share leaves marine open to rate swings. Onshore margin is 9.85% of revenue after product and operating costs and moves with crude marketing spreads and sulfur prices. Margins are therefore resilient to cost inflation but not to volume loss; the credit implication is that EBITDA is more sensitive to offshore throughput than to any cost lever. facts.label: Capital intensity and cash conversion
facts.text: Capital payments fell from USD 620.019 million in FY2023 to USD 108.776 million over the last twelve months as the CHOPS expansion and SYNC pipeline finished and the Shenandoah and Salamanca platforms started production, and maintenance capital spending of USD 75.6 million in the nine months is mainly marine. Operating cash flow less capital payments turned from deficits in FY2023 and FY2024 to USD 342,904 thousand, or 10.70% of total debt, over the last twelve months, and USD 283,091 thousand or 8.83% before a working-capital inflow. Distributions to common, preferred and minority holders net of minority contributions took USD 188,594 thousand, leaving USD 94,497 thousand before working capital, and the preferred redemptions of USD 221,594 thousand were funded in part by new borrowing. Capex flexibility is good because growth spending is complete and distributions are discretionary, so EBITDA converts to cash that can service debt, but only a small part has been used to reduce debt so far. facts.label: PEST analysis, credit-translated
facts.text: Regulation and weather are material and the rest of the political, economic, social and technological headings are not primary credit drivers on the supplied evidence. Federal regulation of tariffs and of pipeline integrity applies to the pipelines, the Jones Act protects marine competition, and management points to the Iranian situation and renewed imports from Venezuela as drivers of onshore dislocations that may fade, while the earnings release lists tariffs and military conflicts among its risks. Weather is a direct operating risk: early-October hurricane disruption cost about four days of offshore service, and the annual report notes that virtually all operations are exposed to storms. Commodity prices matter to the credit through producer drilling decisions rather than through direct exposure, because offshore fees limit direct exposure to price. Most debt is fixed rate; the floating-rate exposure is the receivables facility and any revolver borrowing, which is small at present. facts.label: Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds
facts.text: Over the next 12 to 24 months the offshore recovery is the swing factor. Two Monument wells are due by the end of the first quarter of 2027 or in the first half, a fifth Shenandoah well by the end of 2027, and two rigs are drilling wells for the Salamanca facility; this supports volumes and offshore margin if completed on time, and leaves the fourth quarter of 2026 near or below the low end of guidance. Marine has near-full utilization, robust spot rates and no major dry-docking until 2027, a tailwind for term renewals; onshore benefits from dislocations that management says could last into 2027. Headwinds are producer underperformance, hurricane season, the covenant step-ups from 2027 and the 2029 note test in October 2028. Over three to five years the franchise benefits from two new rigs expected to enter service and from known discoveries awaiting development, but contract floors decline each year after 2027, so earnings rest more on producer volumes. For credit, the next year decides whether leverage falls on earnings alone or whether debt must be repaid to keep the covenant cushion. Marine has near-full utilization, robust spot rates and no major dry-docking until 2027, a tailwind for term renewals; onshore benefits from dislocations that management says could last into 2027. Headwinds are producer underperformance, hurricane season, the covenant step-ups from 2027 and the 2029 note test in October 2028. Over three to five years the franchise benefits from two new rigs expected to enter service and from known discoveries awaiting development, but contract floors decline each year after 2027, so earnings rest more on producer volumes. For credit, the next year decides whether leverage falls on earnings alone or whether debt must be repaid to keep the covenant cushion.

facts.label: Qualitative downside scenario
facts.text: The scenario starts with producer underperformance that outlasts management's timetable: Shenandoah stays at its minimum commitment, legacy fields remain curtailed, the Monument wells slip beyond the first half of 2027, and a weak hurricane season adds shut-ins. The first operational break is offshore volume, because offshore margin falls almost one for one once volumes are below the contract floors, and the floors cover only 27.51% of last-twelve-months offshore revenue in 2027. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA with fixed interest: a fall of 12.98% in last-twelve-months EBITDA would put statement-derived leverage at 5.75x and a fall of 16.94% would put cash interest cover at 2.00x, which are reference points at the covenant levels on statement-based measures, not a covenant test, and the 2.15x and 2.25x levels are reached at falls of 10.71% and 6.56%. A fall of 16.94% equals 24.84% of offshore revenue less operating costs, so the scenario requires roughly a quarter of the offshore margin to disappear. The liquidity, leverage and refinancing consequence is that availability under the revolver would depend on covenant compliance and the October 2028 test, so the partnership would need to cut distributions, hold back preferred purchases and refinance the 2029 notes early. Management levers are real: growth capital spending is finished, distributions are discretionary, and USD 894.4 million of revolver availability can bridge a few quarters. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis before 2029, but not sufficient to keep leverage falling if volumes stay at the third-quarter level through 2027. The observable triggers are Shenandoah staying at its minimum commitment after the Monument wells connect, guidance missed at the low end, and revolver borrowing used to pay distributions. The primary downside path is a prolonged offshore volume shortfall that lifts leverage and lowers coverage while the covenant levels tighten. facts.label: Overall credit view
facts.text: Overall, Genesis Energy presents an adequate business profile supported by an irreplaceable offshore pipeline franchise with low capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by 5.00x leverage, 2.41x cash interest cover, producer-dependent volumes and a shareholder-first financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because offshore margins are stable and growth spending is finished, though working capital flattered the latest year. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on offshore volumes recovering in 2027, the covenant timetable and early action on the 2029 notes before the October 2028 test. The primary downside path is a prolonged offshore volume shortfall that lifts leverage and lowers coverage as covenant levels tighten. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, covenant compliance calculations, field-level contract terms and peer and market data. Fundamental credit analysis complete. Top risk: offshore volumes staying below expectations through 2027 while leverage stays above 5x. Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F22; calculation F10; calculation F29

### Bottom line

The supplied filings and releases are sufficient for a financial, business and capital-structure read of Genesis Energy through 30 September 2026, but not for covenant definitions, legal ranking or relative value, because no executed debt documents, ratings or prices were supplied. The three 2026 quarterly results add up exactly to the nine-month totals for Adjusted EBITDA, attributable net income and operating cash flow, so the quarterly series can be used without adjustment.

spans.text: # CP-1 Financial foundation: GENESIS ENERGY LP (gel), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

This is the Financial foundation for GENESIS ENERGY LP (issuer id gel), as of 2026-11-05. The pathway is the credit snapshot, run through Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit. The scope is the normalised statements, debt, liquidity, leverage and coverage of Genesis Energy, L.P. and its consolidated subsidiaries from the seven supplied documents.
## Sources

| EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the second quarter of 2026 | 2026-08-06 (release date) | e543ee3e3398ce04f2a72be94919a9105edf4587f39625f574d75860af788168 | Issuer-stated Adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter of 2026 |

## Findings
### Bottom line
Genesis Energy's leverage fell to 5.00x last-twelve-months EBITDA at 30 September 2026 from 5.77x at the end of 2025, but cash interest cover of 2.41x remains thin.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; calculation K31; calculation K32; calculation K36

The improvement came from higher earnings, not repayment: carrying-value debt rose by USD 159.34 million in the nine months because a receivables facility and a larger note issue helped fund the redemption of preferred units. Revolver availability of USD 894.4 million and the absence of any maturity before 2029 limit near-term refinancing risk. The company's own bank leverage ratio of 5.03x uses a narrower debt definition and a different EBITDA, so it is not comparable with these figures.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–18; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation K6; calculation K17; calculation K19; calculation K25; calculation K32; calculation K36; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Leverage and coverage

Leverage on carrying-value debt fell from 8.89x at the end of 2024 to 5.77x at the end of 2025 and 5.00x at 30 September 2026. The 2024 ratio is not like-for-like: that debt also funded the Alkali business, sold in February 2025 and shown as discontinued, while the EBITDA covers continuing operations only. Gross debt rose in 2026, so the fall to the latest ratio rests on higher earnings over the last twelve months, which creditors need to see sustained, rather than on repayment.

Cash interest cover rose from 1.43x in FY2024 to 1.87x in FY2025 and 2.41x on the last twelve months, against a minimum covenant of 2.00x that is measured on the credit agreement's own definitions and therefore cannot be tested from these figures.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 166–167; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 210; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 29; calculation K6; calculation K7; calculation K30; calculation K31; calculation K32; calculation K33; calculation K34; calculation K35; calculation K36; calculation K37
### Cash flow quality

Operating cash flow for the nine months of 2026 was helped by a working-capital inflow that reversed the outflow of the nine months of 2025, so it is not a clean run-rate. Cash paid for fixed and intangible assets fell sharply after the completion of the offshore growth projects in 2025, which is why earnings less capital expenditure covers cash interest 2.00x on the last twelve months against 1.21x in FY2025. Cash flow statements include the discontinued Alkali business until its sale on 2025-02-28, so annual and nine-month 2025 figures are on a total-company basis.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 5; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 28; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 168–169; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 52–53; calculation K8; calculation K9; calculation K10; calculation K38; calculation K39
### Liquidity and maturities

The USD 99.5 million receivables facility is fully drawn and is carried as a current borrowing although it expires in 2029. No note matures before January 2029, the revolver matures in March 2031 with an earlier springing date if more than USD 150 million of the 2029 notes or 2030 notes remain outstanding at the dates stated, and the revolver is undrawn. Liquidity is cash of USD 41,477 thousand plus revolver availability of USD 894.4 million after letters of credit.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 49; calculation K19; calculation K20
### Definitions and data quality

The statements-based EBITDA includes the share of noncontrolling interests and equity earnings, while the release's EBITDA and Adjusted EBITDA are net to Genesis' ownership interest; the two bases differ by the noncontrolling interest and accretion lines. Adjusted EBITDA for the nine months of 2026 also keeps a gain of USD 17,436 thousand on the sale of offshore gas assets, which the cash flow reconciliation adds back and the Select Items do not remove. Total debt includes the receivables facility, which the issuer's Adjusted Debt excludes, and the issuer's Adjusted Debt also deducts an inventory financing amount although the revolver is undrawn.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, pages 9–11; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; calculation K26; calculation K27

spans.text: # CP-1A Business & governance: GENESIS ENERGY LP (gel), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

This is the Business & governance fact pack for GENESIS ENERGY LP (issuer id gel), as of 2026-11-05. The pathway is the credit snapshot, run through Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit. The scope is the business, ownership, governance, capital-allocation and 2026 financing facts that matter to a creditor, drawn from the seven supplied documents.
## Sources

## Findings
### Bottom line

Genesis Energy is a Gulf of America pipeline franchise with contracted but producer-dependent volumes, and in 2026 the partnership is directing improved cash flow to retiring preferred units and raising distributions while gross debt rises, which keeps noteholders reliant on continued offshore throughput.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 22; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; calculation B5; calculation B7; calculation B8

Offshore pipelines produced 67.74% of nine-month 2026 Segment Margin, and in the third quarter Shenandoah volumes fell below the minimum commitment, so only the minimum was recognised. Voting control rests with Class B units held mainly by one family, and the preferred investors keep a board observer right while they hold enough of the class. The executed debt documents that would bind these choices were not supplied, so the limits on distributions and further preferred purchases are not established.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 6; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 128–129; calculation B1; calculation B8; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Key findings

- The offshore pipeline segment is the credit, and it is concentrated in a few producer-operated fields. It supplied 66.75% of FY2025 Segment Margin and 67.74% of the nine months of 2026, on contracts with minimum volume commitments and tiered fees, but its Segment Margin fell 3.50% in the third quarter because Shenandoah and legacy fields underperformed. The segment's results therefore track producer drilling, not the partnership's own spending, which is now complete.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 90; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation B1; calculation B4; calculation B10

- Marine and onshore services diversify earnings but are small and cyclical. They supplied 17.38% and 14.87% of nine-month Segment Margin; marine utilization was high and onshore volumes rose on Gulf-produced crude and market dislocations that management itself calls possibly non-recurring.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation B2; calculation B3

- Control is concentrated and creditors have no governance voice. Class B units elect the whole board, one family holds 76.9% of them and can appoint up to three directors, and the partnership has chosen not to follow listing rules on independent nominating and compensation committees. Creditors rely on contract terms, which are not supplied, rather than on governance.

- Preferred equity is shrinking quickly and its remaining holders keep influence. The partnership bought back 41.15% of the preferred units outstanding at the end of 2025 for USD 221,594 thousand in three purchases, at prices from the USD 33.71 issue price to USD 34.38. Two funds held 91.2% of the class at the end of 2025, and the filings do not say who sold. The remaining units carry an 11.24% coupon, and the initial purchasers keep a board observer right while they hold USD 200 million of the class.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 129; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 152; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 21–22; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 48; calculation B5; calculation B6; calculation B14

- Capital allocation has turned from growth to returns. Growth capital fell 80.93% in the nine months, the common distribution is 21.21% above the level of a year ago, and a small common unit repurchase was made, while gross debt rose by USD 159.34 million. The pattern favours equity holders over debt reduction in 2026 and depends on the offshore volumes holding.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 51–52; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 19; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 166; calculation B7; calculation B9; calculation B11

- The 2026 financing was creditor-neutral to positive on tenor, with the nearest note maturity pushed to January 2029 and a larger revolver, but it also widened flexibility for investments and added a secured receivables facility whose receivables are ring-fenced from other creditors.
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is contractual and liquidity support: management says nine of sixteen active deepwater rigs work leases dedicated to flow through its facilities, four new high-impact wells are due to restore volumes, the revolver has USD 894.4 million available and no debt matures before 2029. The view would soften if offshore volumes returned above the minimum commitments for several quarters and the executed debt documents showed tight limits on distributions and preferred purchases. It would harden if volumes stayed weak into 2027, guidance for the year were missed, or distributions and preferred purchases continued to be funded with new debt.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 17–18; calculation B12; Source readiness (CP-0)
### Limitations

- The credit agreement and indentures were not supplied, so the conclusion that distributions and preferred purchases may continue to be debt-funded is untested against restricted-payment limits and could be wrong either way.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–19; Source readiness (CP-0)

- Ownership data are dated 2026-02-18 for common units and the end of 2025 for preferred units, and the 2026 preferred sellers are unnamed, so the conclusion about who now holds influence over the remaining preferred units is not established and may already have changed.
- The partnership's organizational chart in the annual report is an image whose content was not extracted, so the entity-level picture behind the control conclusion rests on narrative notes only.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 9; Source readiness (CP-0)
- Outlook statements are management's own and give no dollar guidance range, so the conclusion that offshore volumes will recover rests on producer plans that the partnership does not control.
Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-05-07_a90ex9918kearnings_q12026.htm.jsonl, page 1

### Company profile

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On 2026-03-04 the partnership issued USD 750.0 million of senior unsecured notes due 2034 and signed an Eighth Amended and Restated Credit Agreement that lifted revolver capacity from USD 800 million to USD 900 million and moved its maturity to 2031. Net proceeds of about USD 735.9 million bought USD 416.1 million of the 2028 notes in a tender that ended on 2026-03-20 and redeemed the remaining USD 263.3 million on 2026-03-22, with the rest helping to fund a preferred unit purchase on 2026-03-06. The partnership recorded a loss of USD 3.4 million on the tender premium, fees and written-off costs.

On 2026-06-26 it signed a three-year USD 99.5 million receivables securitization facility priced at Term SOFR plus 1.375%, borrowed through a bankruptcy-remote subsidiary whose receivables are not available to other creditors, and the facility is fully drawn. On 2026-06-03 it sold non-core natural gas pipeline and platform assets in the offshore segment for USD 95.0 million, recognising a gain of USD 17,436 thousand, and used the proceeds to buy preferred units on 2026-06-08.

Across 2026 the partnership bought preferred units on three dates for USD 221,594 thousand, which cut the class by 41.15%, and paid common distributions of USD 0.20 per unit for the second and third quarters. Its earlier 2025 transactions were the sale of the Alkali business for USD 1,425 million gross, the redemption of the 2027 notes, and a purchase of preferred units for USD 262.5 million. spans.text: # CP-2 Fundamental credit: GENESIS ENERGY LP (gel), as of 2026-11-05
## Request

This is the Fundamental credit assessment for GENESIS ENERGY LP (issuer id gel), as of 2026-11-05. The pathway is the credit snapshot, run through Source readiness, Financial foundation, Business & governance and Fundamental credit. The scope is the overall credit profile of Genesis Energy, L.P., its strongest support and its primary downside, drawn from the seven supplied documents and the three earlier modules.
## Sources
| Source | Document | Document date | sha256 | Use |

| 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl | Annual report on Form 10-K for the year ended 31 December 2025 | 2026-02-18 (signature date) | ccb89bebbe1f6460b65cf41694753b9c46d6084fa3c93974775412b94a4649f8 | Offshore pipeline capacity and contract terms, marine contract mix, customer concentration, competition, revenue recognition, FY2023 to FY2025 statements |

| 10-Q_2026-03-31_gel-20260331.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 31 March 2026 | 2026-05-07 (signature date) | 25844b5fb23f8fb7e6ed5e3ecd46a1d84117c9d80e65e2ca8d092544b9bdbfa5 | Read for continuity of the 2026 financing events; no figure is taken from it in this module |

| 10-Q_2026-06-30_gel-20260630.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 | 2026-08-06 (signature date) | abd4ada77d59922e6f0bafe2fa139c2cc408c45768d2e839399c3eb81593724d | Read for continuity of the 2026 events; no figure is taken from it in this module |

| 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl | Quarterly report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended 30 September 2026 | 2026-11-05 (signature date) | b8ecb63006d005d24876220dffec5b55d573a9ed4071631f5d65780aeca8bd64 | Nine-month 2026 statements, segment results, remaining contract value, credit agreement terms and covenant levels, debt, distributions, offshore outlook |

| EX-99.1_2026-05-07_a90ex9918kearnings_q12026.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the first quarter of 2026 | 2026-05-07 (release date) | dacbb1e9e5b2b770bd5cf7b317240e0ada11d6948f3a4f941eec0c98544a6e5d | Shenandoah effect on 2026 Segment Margin against original guidance |

| EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the second quarter of 2026 | 2026-08-06 (release date) | e543ee3e3398ce04f2a72be94919a9105edf4587f39625f574d75860af788168 | Lowered 2026 guidance wording, reliance on operator information, savings estimates |

| EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl | Earnings release (Exhibit 99.1) for the third quarter of 2026 | 2026-11-05 (release date) | c64ffa295db0861a2124c70f86ea927a2ba296a55d07643ed60b307a769d0d5c | Operating volumes, distribution coverage, bank leverage ratio, management outlook for offshore, marine and onshore |
| Handoff | Module | sha256 | Use |
| Source readiness | CP-0 | 0cec93cd51f25e659237603d1a0cde0e7644125a72d3dd17f2e2dcf35f1c9f9f | Source limits, perimeter and the gap list |
| Financial foundation | CP-1 | 99a7e254c571772cd99385dc6ef197db736aab54e3725ca543cd1fb5ae27cf56 | Statements, debt, liquidity, leverage, coverage and the post-balance-sheet adjustments |
| Business & governance | CP-1A | 42b4e370829352ea3bc51a2b1c37c0acd77fc13f4fa4af84449bba378a2e97fb | Business model, ownership, control, capital allocation and 2026 financing events |
## Findings
### Bottom line

Genesis Energy is a levered but liquid midstream credit whose offshore pipeline franchise supports debt service, yet deleveraging now depends on offshore volumes recovering in 2027, not on debt repayment.
Basis: Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F1; calculation F22

Total debt is 5.00x last-twelve-months EBITDA and cash interest cover is 2.41x, so a volume miss reaches coverage quickly. Revolver availability of USD 894.4 million and no maturity before 2029 give time to prove the recovery, while the 2027 covenant step-ups, debt-funded distributions and the 2029 note refinancing are the points to watch.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 16–18; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation F22; calculation F30; calculation F28
### Key findings

- The offshore pipeline franchise is the main support of the credit and its main concentration. It earned 67.74% of nine-month 2026 Segment Margin on fee-based, life-of-lease dedications, and its revenue less operating costs has stayed between 71.05% and 74.87% of revenue since FY2023, so volume rather than cost sets its earnings. Throughput can grow without new spending: CHOPS ran at 66.39% of design capacity in the third quarter, and management says nine of the sixteen active deepwater rigs work leases dedicated to its facilities. Creditors hold a high-margin, low-capital cash stream whose size depends on producers' drilling.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 16; 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 20; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 8; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; calculation F1; calculation F2; calculation F3; calculation F4; calculation F5; calculation F9

- Contract protection is real but short. Fixed and minimum-based offshore contract value still to be recognised equals 27.51% of last-twelve-months offshore revenue for 2027 and 13.91% for 2028, so earnings beyond 2028 rest mainly on producer volumes. The third quarter showed the floor at work: Shenandoah volumes fell below the minimum commitment and only the minimum was recognised, yet offshore Segment Margin still fell 3.50% in the quarter although it is 20.73% higher over the nine months.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 6; calculation F10; calculation F7; calculation F6

- Expectations for 2026 earnings have eased at each of the three 2026 releases, which makes producer-sourced forecasting the weak point of the credit. The first-quarter release put Shenandoah at USD 12 million to USD 15 million less Segment Margin than original guidance and still aimed for the midpoint, the second said towards the lower end, and the third said near, or possibly below, the low end, with lower volumes from a couple of deepwater facilities expected into early 2027 until four new wells are completed. Management states that it relies heavily on operator information, so the recovery depends on well completions that Genesis does not control.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-05-07_a90ex9918kearnings_q12026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 6; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; calculation F33

- Leverage has improved on earnings, not repayment, and coverage stays thin. Total debt is 5.00x last-twelve-months EBITDA against 5.77x at the end of 2025 and 8.89x at the end of 2024, but carrying-value debt rose by USD 159.34 million in 2026. Net debt is 4.94x, and pro forma 4.98x after the common distribution payable on 2026-11-13 and 4.95x after the preferred distribution payable the same day, each taken separately. Cash interest cover is 2.41x and falls to 2.14x once distributions to minority holders are deducted from EBITDA, because the EBITDA used here includes their share.

Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 20; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F22; calculation F23; calculation F21; calculation F26

- Cash conversion has improved because growth spending ended, but working capital flatters the latest year. Operating cash flow less capital payments is USD 342,904 thousand over the last twelve months against USD 65,938 thousand in FY2025 and deficits in FY2024 and FY2023; excluding the working-capital inflow of USD 59,813 thousand it is USD 283,091 thousand. After net distributions to common, preferred and minority holders, USD 94,497 thousand remains before working capital, so debt reduction is possible but not yet demonstrated.
Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, pages 168–169; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 5–6; calculation F16; calculation F17; calculation F18; calculation F19

- Liquidity is adequate for about two years, and the real refinancing deadline is earlier than the note maturity. Revolver availability of USD 894.4 million is 1.49x the 2029 notes and liquidity is 3.52x last-twelve-months cash interest, and no note matures before 2029. But the credit agreement matures on 2028-10-16 if more than USD 150 million of the 2029 notes remain outstanding then, and the 2029 and 2030 maturities together are 36.91% of principal, so the notes must be addressed while leverage is above 5x.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 14–18; calculation F28; calculation F27; calculation F29

- Financial policy is the weakest dimension because cash is going to equity before debt. The partnership retired 41.15% of the preferred units for USD 221,594 thousand and raised the common distribution 21.21% above the level of a year ago while total debt rose, and it estimates that the 2026 financing steps cut its annual cost of capital by about USD 25 million. The saving is real, since the preferred coupon exceeds the cost of the new notes, but creditors carry more senior claims against the same earnings.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; EX-99.1_2026-08-06_a90ex9918kearnings_q22026.htm.jsonl, page 2; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation F21; calculation F33

- Covenant terms tighten on a published timetable and compliance is not confirmed. The issuer's own bank ratio is 5.03x against a 5.75x maximum that falls to 5.50x after 2027, the minimum interest coverage rises from 2.00x to 2.15x in 2027 and 2.25x after that, and senior secured leverage is capped at 2.50x with the revolver undrawn. No 2026 filing states compliance, so these terms frame the downside rather than measure it.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 17; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 11; calculation F30

- Marine and onshore services diversify earnings but add little stability. Marine earned 17.38% and onshore 14.87% of nine-month Segment Margin; 77% of marine revenue was on term contracts in FY2025 and barge utilization is near full, while onshore keeps only 9.85% of revenue after product and operating costs and management ties its upside to market dislocations that could last into 2027.

Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_gel-20251231.htm.jsonl, page 22; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 8; calculation F13; calculation F14; calculation F12
### Contrary evidence and what would change the view

The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that the franchise is under-used rather than impaired. Offshore Segment Margin rose 20.73% over the nine months as two new floating production units started, nine of the sixteen active deepwater rigs work leases dedicated to Genesis facilities, four new high-impact wells are expected to restore volumes from early 2027, and the issuer covered its third-quarter common distribution 1.58x after interest, maintenance capital and preferred distributions. Leverage has also fallen from 8.89x to 5.00x in two years, the issuer's own ratio is 0.72x inside its covenant maximum, and no debt matures until 2029.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 1; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 26; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation F6; calculation F15; calculation F22; calculation F30

The view would improve if Shenandoah volumes moved back above the minimum commitment for two consecutive quarters after the Monument wells connect, if absolute debt fell rather than rose, and if the 2029 notes were refinanced well before the October 2028 test. It would worsen if full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA came in below the low end of guidance, if the issuer's bank ratio rose above 5.03x, if further preferred purchases or distribution increases were funded with new borrowing, or if fewer than nine of the sixteen active rigs worked dedicated leases.

Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 16; calculation F30; calculation F29
### Limitations

- Remaining contract value is disclosed only in total by year, with no field, customer or minimum-commitment amount, so the conclusion that contracts floor offshore earnings for about two years cannot be tested for Shenandoah or any other field.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 41; calculation F10

- Leverage and coverage are built from statement lines that include the minority holders' share of earnings, while the issuer's own measures net it out, so the conclusion that coverage is thin could be understated or overstated by the difference between the two definitions.
Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_gel-20260930.htm.jsonl, page 3; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_a90ex9918kearnings_q32026.htm.jsonl, page 11; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation F26

### Company description and credit linkage

Genesis Energy is a Houston-based midstream partnership that earns fees in three businesses: offshore crude oil and natural gas pipelines in the Gulf of America, a U.S.-flag Jones Act marine fleet, and onshore crude pipelines with sulfur services on the Gulf Coast. Offshore fees are charged per barrel or under capacity arrangements that limit direct exposure to commodity prices, most production handled is under life-of-lease commitments, and 77% of marine revenue was on term contracts in FY2025. That gives the group visible cash flow while producers keep producing, but only about 27.51% of last-twelve-months offshore revenue is fixed or minimum-based for 2027, so visibility fades after 2028. Onshore revenue is largely crude marketing sales that carry thin margins. Debt service capacity is therefore supported by the offshore fee stream, liquidity is preserved by the end of growth spending, and refinancing confidence depends on offshore volumes holding while leverage is above 5x.

### Ownership and group structure

Genesis Energy, L.P. is a listed partnership whose general partner it owns outright. Class B units elect the whole board, one family holds 76.9% of them and can appoint up to three directors, and holders of the preferred units keep a board observer right while they hold enough of the class. The partnership has chosen not to follow listing rules on independent nominating and compensation committees. The notes are guaranteed by the domestic guarantor subsidiaries, while the receivables facility sits in a bankruptcy-remote vehicle outside the guarantor group and its receivables are not available to other creditors. A financial party owns the remaining 36% of CHOPS and the consolidated Independence Hub also carries a noncontrolling interest, so part of consolidated EBITDA leaves the group as distributions to those holders. The credit implication is that control is concentrated, creditors have no governance voice, the 2026 pattern favours equity returns, and the structurally senior claims are the USD 99.5 million receivables facility and minority distributions equal to 11.32% of EBITDA.

### Revenue drivers and pricing power

Offshore revenue is volume-driven: fees are fixed per unit of volume under contracts or regulated tariffs, some contracts add capacity-reservation fees, and tiered fees step with cumulative throughput, so earnings follow producers' well performance and the number of rigs that can drill. The mechanism showed in the third quarter, when oil volumes were 0.99% lower and gas volumes 31.98% lower than a year earlier, Shenandoah fell below its minimum commitment and offshore Segment Margin fell 3.50%, although nine-month oil volumes were still 13.26% higher. For credit, offshore revenue is partly predictable through 2028, cyclical with drilling activity, concentrated by field, and exposed to hurricanes; pricing is set by contract and tariff, so growth comes from volume rather than price. Marine revenue is 77% term and 23% spot, utilization is near full and management reports robust spot rates, which supports renewals. Onshore pipeline volumes rose 35.49% in the third quarter, and the sulfur business holds 11 contracts with about two years remaining on average, so onshore is recurring in part but its upside is tied to dislocations. No single customer exceeded 10% of revenue in 2025, although Shell reached 11% in 2024, so customer concentration is moderate and the larger concentration is in producers behind a few fields.

### Cost structure and margin resilience

The offshore cost base is small relative to revenue and, on the evidence of a steady margin, largely fixed, so revenue less operating costs held between 71.05% and 74.87% of revenue from FY2023 to the last twelve months; that margin can be defended under volume pressure only until volumes fall below minimum commitments, after which each lost barrel falls almost entirely to EBITDA. Marine margin after operating costs slipped from 38.87% in FY2024 to 33.52% over the last twelve months; nine-month Segment Margin fell 3.70% on planned dry-docking days, although the third quarter rose 12.16%, and rebilled fuel and other costs that pass through enlarge revenue and costs together, so the percentage understates cash margin. The 23% spot share leaves marine open to rate swings. Onshore margin is 9.85% of revenue after product and operating costs and moves with crude marketing spreads and sulfur prices. Margins are therefore resilient to cost inflation but not to volume loss; the credit implication is that EBITDA is more sensitive to offshore throughput than to any cost lever.

### Porter's five forces

Competitive rivalry is moderate. Offshore pipelines compete on proximity, cost of connection, capacity, rates and onshore access, and producers could build their own handling facilities; marine carriers compete with other pipelines, rail and trucking. Dedicated leases reduce the risk for offshore, so rivalry matters most for marine and onshore margins.

The threat of new entrants is low: the annual report cites high capital costs, tariff regulation and the cost of acquiring rights-of-way as barriers for pipelines, management calls its deepwater system irreplaceable, and the Jones Act restricts domestic marine capacity to U.S.-built, U.S.-owned vessels; this supports the stability of fees rather than their growth.

### PEST analysis, credit-translated

Regulation and weather are material and the rest of the political, economic, social and technological headings are not primary credit drivers on the supplied evidence. Federal regulation of tariffs and of pipeline integrity applies to the pipelines, the Jones Act protects marine competition, and management points to the Iranian situation and renewed imports from Venezuela as drivers of onshore dislocations that may fade, while the earnings release lists tariffs and military conflicts among its risks. Weather is a direct operating risk: early-October hurricane disruption cost about four days of offshore service, and the annual report notes that virtually all operations are exposed to storms. Commodity prices matter to the credit through producer drilling decisions rather than through direct exposure, because offshore fees limit direct exposure to price. Most debt is fixed rate; the floating-rate exposure is the receivables facility and any revolver borrowing, which is small at present.

### Outlook, tailwinds and headwinds

Over the next 12 to 24 months the offshore recovery is the swing factor. Two Monument wells are due by the end of the first quarter of 2027 or in the first half, a fifth Shenandoah well by the end of 2027, and two rigs are drilling wells for the Salamanca facility; this supports volumes and offshore margin if completed on time, and leaves the fourth quarter of 2026 near or below the low end of guidance. Marine has near-full utilization, robust spot rates and no major dry-docking until 2027, a tailwind for term renewals; onshore benefits from dislocations that management says could last into 2027. Headwinds are producer underperformance, hurricane season, the covenant step-ups from 2027 and the 2029 note test in October 2028. Over three to five years the franchise benefits from two new rigs expected to enter service and from known discoveries awaiting development, but contract floors decline each year after 2027, so earnings rest more on producer volumes. For credit, the next year decides whether leverage falls on earnings alone or whether debt must be repaid to keep the covenant cushion.

### Qualitative downside scenario

The scenario starts with producer underperformance that outlasts management's timetable: Shenandoah stays at its minimum commitment, legacy fields remain curtailed, the Monument wells slip beyond the first half of 2027, and a weak hurricane season adds shut-ins. The first operational break is offshore volume, because offshore margin falls almost one for one once volumes are below the contract floors, and the floors cover only 27.51% of last-twelve-months offshore revenue in 2027. The financial transmission is lower EBITDA with fixed interest: a fall of 12.98% in last-twelve-months EBITDA would put statement-derived leverage at 5.75x and a fall of 16.94% would put cash interest cover at 2.00x, which are reference points at the covenant levels on statement-based measures, not a covenant test, and the 2.15x and 2.25x levels are reached at falls of 10.71% and 6.56%. A fall of 16.94% equals 24.84% of offshore revenue less operating costs, so the scenario requires roughly a quarter of the offshore margin to disappear. The liquidity, leverage and refinancing consequence is that availability under the revolver would depend on covenant compliance and the October 2028 test, so the partnership would need to cut distributions, hold back preferred purchases and refinance the 2029 notes early. Management levers are real: growth capital spending is finished, distributions are discretionary, and USD 894.4 million of revolver availability can bridge a few quarters. Resilience therefore appears sufficient to avoid a liquidity crisis before 2029, but not sufficient to keep leverage falling if volumes stay at the third-quarter level through 2027. The observable triggers are Shenandoah staying at its minimum commitment after the Monument wells connect, guidance missed at the low end, and revolver borrowing used to pay distributions. The primary downside path is a prolonged offshore volume shortfall that lifts leverage and lowers coverage while the covenant levels tighten.

### Overall credit view

Overall, Genesis Energy presents an adequate business profile supported by an irreplaceable offshore pipeline franchise with low capital needs, but credit quality is constrained by 5.00x leverage, 2.41x cash interest cover, producer-dependent volumes and a shareholder-first financial policy. Cash-flow durability appears adequate because offshore margins are stable and growth spending is finished, though working capital flattered the latest year. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on offshore volumes recovering in 2027, the covenant timetable and early action on the 2029 notes before the October 2028 test. The primary downside path is a prolonged offshore volume shortfall that lifts leverage and lowers coverage as covenant levels tighten. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, covenant compliance calculations, field-level contract terms and peer and market data. Fundamental credit analysis complete. Top risk: offshore volumes staying below expectations through 2027 while leverage stays above 5x.

## Gaps

- High: no covenant compliance statement or calculation is supplied for any 2026 quarter and the executed credit agreement is not supplied, so covenant capacity is not calculated here; the reference points in the downside scenario are on statement-based measures only. Action: obtain the credit agreement and a compliance certificate.

- High: the amount, term and field of each minimum volume commitment, including Shenandoah, are not disclosed, so the size of the contract floor under the offshore volume shortfall is not established. Action: obtain the contract summaries or the operator's disclosure.

- Medium: the 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance range in dollars, the year-end call text and the dollar effect of the October 2026 hurricane disruption and facility curtailment are not supplied, so the fourth-quarter shortfall is not quantified. Action: obtain the fourth-quarter 2025 release and the call text.

- Medium: the Monument tieback is dated at the end of the first quarter of 2027 in the earnings release and in the first half of 2027 in the quarterly report; both are management statements and the difference is not resolved. Action: ask the operator for the first-oil date.

- Medium: no peer, rating, price or spread data were supplied, so the comparison with other leveraged midstream issuers, relative value and refinancing cost at current market terms are not assessed. Action: obtain market data and peer filings.

- Low: customer concentration is reported only as no single customer above 10% of revenue in 2025, and producer concentration by field is not disclosed. Action: obtain customer and field detail if sizing exposure.

- Low: floating-rate exposure is limited to the receivables facility and any revolver use, and no interest rate hedge is described in the supplied documents; the effect of a rate move is not calculated. Action: none needed unless the revolver is drawn.
